name: vn-en-eval-set-v1
description: 100 Vietnamese-learner English correction pairs for AI tutor evaluation. Each entry has an ungrammatical input sentence, the expected natural correction, error classification tags, tone/register judgment, CEFR difficulty level, and the Vietnamese source interference pattern.

entries.input: I go to the market yesterday.
entries.expected: I went to the market yesterday.
entries.vietlishPattern: hôm qua tôi đi → time word marks past tense in Vietnamese; verb root unchanged

entries.input: She study very hard last night.
entries.expected: She studied very hard last night.
entries.vietlishPattern: đêm qua cô ấy học → past event, verb not inflected

entries.input: Yesterday they play football in the park.
entries.expected: Yesterday they played football in the park.
entries.vietlishPattern: hôm qua họ chơi → verb root unchanged with past time adverb

entries.input: He tell me the secret this morning.
entries.expected: He told me the secret this morning.
entries.vietlishPattern: sáng nay anh ấy nói → irregular past form 'told' not acquired

entries.input: I not go to school yesterday because I am sick.
entries.expected: I did not go to school yesterday because I was sick.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi không đi học hôm qua → negation without auxiliary 'did'; present copula carried into past clause

entries.input: We eat dinner already, thank you.
entries.expected: We have already eaten dinner, thank you.
entries.vietlishPattern: chúng tôi đã ăn cơm rồi → 'đã...rồi' completion marker not mapped to present perfect; 'already' placed post-verb

entries.input: She already finish the report.
entries.expected: She has already finished the report.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy đã làm xong báo cáo → 'đã' perfective marker triggers simple past rather than present perfect

entries.input: Have you eat lunch?
entries.expected: Have you eaten lunch?
entries.vietlishPattern: bạn đã ăn trưa chưa → 'chưa' triggers perfect question structure but past participle 'eaten' not inflected

entries.input: Did she already left?
entries.expected: Has she already left?
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy đã đi rồi chưa → 'did' + past participle confusion; completion requires present perfect

entries.input: I know him since three years.
entries.expected: I have known him for three years.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi quen anh ấy được ba năm → duration-from-past-to-present requires present perfect; 'since' used where 'for' (duration) needed

entries.input: When I arrive home, he already eat dinner.
entries.expected: When I arrived home, he had already eaten dinner.
entries.vietlishPattern: khi tôi về thì anh ấy đã ăn rồi → past perfect for prior-completed event not used; verb roots unchanged

entries.input: I am live in Hanoi for ten years.
entries.expected: I have been living in Hanoi for ten years.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi đang sống ở Hà Nội được mười năm → progressive 'đang' mapped to 'am'; duration from past needs perfect continuous

entries.input: She tell me she will come, but she didn't.
entries.expected: She told me she would come, but she didn't.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy nói sẽ đến → reported speech: 'sẽ' (future) not backshifted to 'would'; past tense 'told' also missed

entries.input: By next year I will finish my degree.
entries.expected: By next year I will have finished my degree.
entries.vietlishPattern: sang năm tôi sẽ hoàn thành bằng cấp → future perfect (will + have + past participle) not distinguished from simple future

entries.input: He study English since he was a child.
entries.expected: He has studied English since he was a child.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy học tiếng Anh từ nhỏ → past-to-present continuity requires present perfect; 'since' clause not cued to perfect in L1

entries.input: I was working here since 2020.
entries.expected: I have been working here since 2020.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi làm ở đây từ năm 2020 → ongoing past-to-present activity: past progressive used instead of present perfect continuous

entries.input: She left before I can say goodbye.
entries.expected: She left before I could say goodbye.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy đã đi trước khi tôi kịp nói lời tạm biệt → modal 'can' not backshifted to 'could' in past sequence

entries.input: He is go to work every day.
entries.expected: He goes to work every day.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy đi làm mỗi ngày → 'đang đi' (progressive) confused with 'is go'; habitual action needs simple present

entries.input: I will go to the cinema yesterday.
entries.expected: I went to the cinema yesterday.
entries.vietlishPattern: hôm qua tôi đi xem phim → 'will' used generically for events; past tense required with past time adverb

entries.input: While I drove home, I thought about the problem.
entries.expected: While I was driving home, I thought about the problem.
entries.vietlishPattern: trong khi tôi đang lái xe → background ongoing action needs past progressive; simple past suggests two completed events

entries.input: She is teacher at my school.
entries.expected: She is a teacher at my school.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy là giáo viên → Vietnamese has no indefinite article; profession 'giáo viên' takes no article in L1

entries.input: He wants to be doctor.
entries.expected: He wants to be a doctor.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy muốn làm bác sĩ → profession after 'to be' requires indefinite article in English

entries.input: I have dog and two cats at home.
entries.expected: I have a dog and two cats at home.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi có một con chó và hai con mèo → 'một' (one) is optional in Vietnamese; singular countable needs 'a' in English

entries.input: Can you open window please?
entries.expected: Can you open the window, please?
entries.vietlishPattern: bạn mở cửa sổ được không → contextually unique referent 'cái cửa sổ' needs definite article; omitted in L1

entries.input: Sun rises in the east every morning.
entries.expected: The sun rises in the east every morning.
entries.vietlishPattern: mặt trời mọc ở hướng đông → unique natural object 'mặt trời' takes definite article in English

entries.input: I go to school by the bus.
entries.expected: I go to school by bus.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi đi học bằng xe buýt → transport collocations 'by bus/car/train' take no article; 'bằng' triggers definite article by analogy

entries.input: She has a long black hair.
entries.expected: She has long black hair.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy có mái tóc dài màu đen → 'tóc' (hair) is mass noun in Vietnamese; treated as countable in English with 'a'

entries.input: The life is full of surprises.
entries.expected: Life is full of surprises.
entries.vietlishPattern: cuộc sống rất bất ngờ → generic abstract noun 'cuộc sống' takes no definite article in English

entries.input: He is playing the football with his friends.
entries.expected: He is playing football with his friends.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy đang chơi bóng đá → sport names take no article in English; definite article added by analogy

entries.input: Please give me a water.
entries.expected: Please give me some water.
entries.vietlishPattern: cho tôi một ly nước → 'nước' (water) is uncountable; 'một' mapped to indefinite 'a'

entries.input: She gave me a good advice.
entries.expected: She gave me some good advice.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy cho tôi một lời khuyên hay → 'advice' is uncountable; 'một lời khuyên' maps to 'a piece of advice', not 'a advice'

entries.input: He is studying the medicine at university.
entries.expected: He is studying medicine at university.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy đang học y khoa → academic field names take no definite article; learner adds 'the' by analogy

entries.input: He is an honest and a hardworking student.
entries.expected: He is an honest and hardworking student.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy là một học sinh trung thực và chăm chỉ → article not shared across coordinated adjectives; each gets 'a/an' by analogy

entries.input: I need the help from my teacher to understand this.
entries.expected: I need help from my teacher to understand this.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi cần sự giúp đỡ từ giáo viên → 'sự giúp đỡ' (noun phrase) triggers definite article; 'help' as abstract noun takes none

entries.input: He is working in the abroad.
entries.expected: He is working abroad.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy đang làm việc ở nước ngoài → 'ở nước ngoài' → 'in the abroad'; 'abroad' is an adverb requiring no preposition or article

entries.input: I am very good in English.
entries.expected: I am very good at English.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi giỏi tiếng Anh → 'giỏi' (good) has no prepositional frame in L1; 'good at' collocates with skills

entries.input: She is waiting me at the café.
entries.expected: She is waiting for me at the café.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy đang đợi tôi → 'đợi' takes direct object in Vietnamese; English 'wait' requires preposition 'for'

entries.input: I arrived to the airport very early.
entries.expected: I arrived at the airport very early.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi đến sân bay rất sớm → 'đến' (to/arrive at) mapped to 'to'; 'arrive at' for enclosed spaces

entries.input: He is very interested about linguistics.
entries.expected: He is very interested in linguistics.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy rất quan tâm đến ngôn ngữ học → 'interested in' collocates with 'in'; 'about' borrowed by analogy with 'curious about'

entries.input: She got married with a businessman.
entries.expected: She got married to a businessman.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy kết hôn với một doanh nhân → 'với' means 'with'; English 'get married to' not acquired

entries.input: He is quite different with his brother.
entries.expected: He is quite different from his brother.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy khác với anh trai → 'với' (with/compared to) mapped to 'with'; 'different from' not in L1 frame

entries.input: Please explain me this grammar rule.
entries.expected: Please explain this grammar rule to me.
entries.vietlishPattern: bạn giải thích cho tôi quy tắc này → 'cho tôi' (to me) placed pre-object in L1; 'explain' takes no indirect object without 'to'

entries.input: I discussed about the project with my boss.
entries.expected: I discussed the project with my boss.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi thảo luận về dự án → 'về' (about) calqued; 'discuss' is transitive in English without 'about'

entries.input: She apologized me for being late.
entries.expected: She apologized to me for being late.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy xin lỗi tôi vì đến muộn → 'xin lỗi' takes direct object in Vietnamese; English 'apologize to' requires 'to'

entries.input: I prefer coffee than tea.
entries.expected: I prefer coffee to tea.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi thích cà phê hơn trà → 'hơn' (more than) mapped to 'than'; 'prefer X to Y' comparison frame not acquired

entries.input: I will contact with you next week.
entries.expected: I will contact you next week.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi sẽ liên lạc với bạn → 'với' (with) translated literally; 'contact' is transitive without preposition

entries.input: She is bored from staying at home all day.
entries.expected: She is bored of staying at home all day.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy chán vì ở nhà cả ngày → 'vì' (because of/from) mapped to 'from'; 'bored of' is the standard collocation

entries.input: He succeeded to finish the project on time.
entries.expected: He succeeded in finishing the project on time.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy thành công trong việc hoàn thành → 'succeed in' + gerund; 'to' used by analogy with 'manage to finish'

entries.input: I am looking forward to meet you.
entries.expected: I am looking forward to meeting you.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi mong được gặp bạn → 'look forward to' + gerund; 'to' misread as infinitive marker → base form used

entries.input: She is responsible of the entire project.
entries.expected: She is responsible for the entire project.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy chịu trách nhiệm về toàn bộ dự án → 'responsible for'; 'of' used by analogy with possession

entries.input: Why you are late today?
entries.expected: Why are you late today?
entries.vietlishPattern: tại sao hôm nay bạn đến muộn → Vietnamese questions add question word to SVO order; no subject-auxiliary inversion

entries.input: Where you go yesterday?
entries.expected: Where did you go yesterday?
entries.vietlishPattern: hôm qua bạn đi đâu → no inversion and no do-support; SVO order with question word prepended

entries.input: What means this word?
entries.expected: What does this word mean?
entries.vietlishPattern: từ này có nghĩa là gì → no do-support or inversion; direct translation of SVO question

entries.input: He always is late for class.
entries.expected: He is always late for class.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy luôn luôn đi học muộn → 'luôn luôn' (always) placed before verb in L1; in English frequency adverb follows 'be'

entries.input: I have a new beautiful blue dress.
entries.expected: I have a beautiful new blue dress.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi có một chiếc váy đẹp mới màu xanh → adjective ordering in English: opinion > age/newness > colour; Vietnamese order is flexible

entries.input: Do you know where is the post office?
entries.expected: Do you know where the post office is?
entries.vietlishPattern: bạn có biết bưu điện ở đâu không → embedded question: direct-question inversion retained; indirect question uses statement order

entries.input: I love very much this country.
entries.expected: I love this country very much.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi rất yêu đất nước này → 'rất' (very much) placed post-verb in L1; 'very much' should follow the object in English

entries.input: She is a woman beautiful and intelligent.
entries.expected: She is a beautiful and intelligent woman.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy là người phụ nữ đẹp và thông minh → in Vietnamese adjectives follow the noun; in English attributive adjectives precede

entries.input: Not only she is smart but also hardworking.
entries.expected: She is not only smart but also hardworking.
entries.vietlishPattern: không chỉ cô ấy thông minh mà còn chăm chỉ → 'không chỉ' sentence-initial placement; English 'not only' precedes the predicates, after the subject

entries.input: I yesterday saw your sister at the market.
entries.expected: I saw your sister at the market yesterday.
entries.vietlishPattern: hôm qua tôi gặp chị bạn → time adverb sentence-initial in L1; standard English position is end of clause

entries.input: She very beautiful, isn't it?
entries.expected: She is very beautiful, isn't she?
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy rất đẹp phải không → copula 'is' omitted; tag 'phải không' → 'isn't it'; tag pronoun should match subject

entries.input: He not here today.
entries.expected: He is not here today.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy không ở đây hôm nay → Vietnamese negative 'không' + location; copula 'is' not required in L1 predicate

entries.input: The food delicious!
entries.expected: The food is delicious!
entries.vietlishPattern: đồ ăn ngon quá → Vietnamese predicative adjective needs no 'là'; copula omitted

entries.input: I very happy to meet you.
entries.expected: I am very happy to meet you.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi rất vui được gặp bạn → 'rất vui' adjective predicate without copula 'là' in L1

entries.input: She boring at the lecture.
entries.expected: She was bored at the lecture.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy cảm thấy chán ở buổi giảng → participial adjective confusion: 'boring' (causes boredom) vs 'bored' (experiences it); copula missing

entries.input: He confuse about the new rule.
entries.expected: He is confused about the new rule.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy bối rối về quy tắc mới → 'bối rối' (confused) → base verb form 'confuse' used without copula or past participle ending

entries.input: The children very exciting about the trip.
entries.expected: The children are very excited about the trip.
entries.vietlishPattern: các em rất hào hứng về chuyến đi → participial adjective confusion + copula omission; 'exciting' (stimulus) vs 'excited' (experiencer)

entries.input: He very confident when he speaks.
entries.expected: He is very confident when he speaks.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy rất tự tin khi nói → adjective predicate without copula

entries.input: We hungry, can we eat now?
entries.expected: We are hungry. Can we eat now?
entries.vietlishPattern: chúng tôi đói, chúng tôi ăn được chưa → stative adjective predicate without 'are'

entries.input: He is very success in his career.
entries.expected: He is very successful in his career.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy rất thành công → 'thành công' (noun/adj in Vietnamese) mapped to noun 'success'; adjective 'successful' needed

entries.input: She has many dog at her house.
entries.expected: She has many dogs at her house.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy có nhiều con chó → Vietnamese nouns do not inflect for number; plural -s not added

entries.input: He gave me three advice about the job.
entries.expected: He gave me three pieces of advice about the job.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy đưa ra ba lời khuyên → 'advice' is uncountable; classifier 'pieces of' required for countable use

entries.input: I need more informations to decide.
entries.expected: I need more information to decide.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi cần thêm thông tin → 'thông tin' treated as countable noun; 'information' is uncountable mass noun in English

entries.input: He bought new furnitures for his apartment.
entries.expected: He bought new furniture for his apartment.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy mua đồ nội thất mới → 'đồ nội thất' treated as countable; 'furniture' is mass noun in English

entries.input: I learned many knowledges from this program.
entries.expected: I gained a lot of knowledge from this program.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi học được nhiều kiến thức → 'kiến thức' treated as countable + 'học kiến thức' → 'gain/acquire knowledge'

entries.input: She had many homeworks to do last night.
entries.expected: She had a lot of homework to do last night.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy có nhiều bài tập về nhà → 'homework' is uncountable; 'nhiều' → 'many' triggers plural form

entries.input: Can you print two papers for the meeting?
entries.expected: Can you print two sheets of paper for the meeting?
entries.vietlishPattern: bạn in cho tôi hai tờ giấy → 'tờ' (sheet/classifier) dropped; 'paper' used as countable

entries.input: I have a good news for you.
entries.expected: I have some good news for you.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi có một tin tốt → 'một' (one) mapped to 'a'; 'news' is uncountable in English

entries.input: The police is looking for the suspect.
entries.expected: The police are looking for the suspect.
entries.vietlishPattern: cảnh sát đang tìm kiếm → 'cảnh sát' is singular collective noun in L1; English 'police' is plural

entries.input: He ate three breads and a bowl of soup.
entries.expected: He ate three bread rolls and a bowl of soup.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy ăn ba cái bánh mì → 'bánh mì' (a discrete bread item) mapped to uncountable 'bread'; classifier needed in English

entries.input: My sister, she is a nurse at the city hospital.
entries.expected: My sister is a nurse at the city hospital.
entries.vietlishPattern: chị tôi, chị ấy là y tá → topic-comment structure re-states topic as pronoun; redundant in English

entries.input: Yesterday I met him mother at the market.
entries.expected: Yesterday I met his mother at the market.
entries.vietlishPattern: hôm qua tôi gặp mẹ của anh ấy → object pronoun 'him' used as possessive; 'his' not yet acquired

entries.input: They enjoyed theirself a lot at the party.
entries.expected: They enjoyed themselves a lot at the party.
entries.vietlishPattern: họ rất vui → reflexive pronoun not required in L1; '-self' form over-regularized to 'theirself'

entries.input: I need to improve me before the exam.
entries.expected: I need to improve myself before the exam.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi cần cải thiện bản thân → 'bản thân' (self) not mapped to reflexive pronoun

entries.input: She told to me that she was coming.
entries.expected: She told me that she was coming.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy nói với tôi → 'với' (with/to) translated as 'to'; 'tell' is ditransitive without 'to'

entries.input: Please open the light, it is too dark.
entries.expected: Please turn on the light, it is too dark.
entries.vietlishPattern: mở đèn lên → 'mở' (open) used for activating lights; English uses 'turn on'

entries.input: Can you close the fan? I am cold.
entries.expected: Can you turn off the fan? I am cold.
entries.vietlishPattern: tắt quạt → 'tắt' (turn off/close off) mapped to 'close'; English uses 'turn off' for appliances

entries.input: I want to make my English more perfect.
entries.expected: I want to improve my English.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi muốn làm tiếng Anh của mình tốt hơn → 'làm cho tốt hơn' → 'make more perfect'; 'perfect' is absolute; 'improve' is the natural verb

entries.input: He is a very high man.
entries.expected: He is a very tall man.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy rất cao → 'cao' means tall (person) or high (position/height); 'high' not used for person's stature

entries.input: She studies very hardly.
entries.expected: She studies very hard.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy học rất chăm chỉ → 'hard' is the adverb; 'hardly' means 'barely'; over-regularized with '-ly'

entries.input: My heart is very hurt when I heard the news.
entries.expected: I was deeply hurt when I heard the news.
entries.vietlishPattern: trái tim tôi đau → body-part metaphor calqued; English prefers psychological subject 'I was hurt'

entries.input: I will try my best to handle this problem.
entries.expected: I will do my best to deal with this problem.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi sẽ cố hết sức để giải quyết vấn đề → 'try one's best' acceptable but marginal; 'do one's best' + 'deal with' are stronger collocations

entries.input: Please kindly be informed that the meeting is cancelled.
entries.expected: Please note that the meeting has been cancelled.
entries.vietlishPattern: kính báo → formal Vietnamese business opening formula; over-translated into English as 'please kindly be informed'

entries.input: I am writing to inquire about the possibility of obtaining your assistance.
entries.expected: I am writing to ask for your help.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi viết thư này để nhờ sự giúp đỡ → formal Vietnamese register calqued into hyper-elevated English; plain business English preferred

entries.input: He speaks English very good.
entries.expected: He speaks English very well.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy nói tiếng Anh rất tốt → 'tốt' (good/well) used as adjective; 'well' needed as manner adverb after verb

entries.input: Although she was sick, but she came to work.
entries.expected: Although she was sick, she came to work.
entries.vietlishPattern: tuy bị bệnh nhưng cô ấy vẫn đi làm → 'tuy...nhưng' double concessive conjunction; English uses one: 'although' replaces both

entries.input: Even though he studied hard, but he failed the exam.
entries.expected: Even though he studied hard, he failed the exam.
entries.vietlishPattern: dù anh ấy học chăm chỉ nhưng vẫn trượt → 'dù...nhưng' double conjunction; one concessive word is enough in English

entries.input: The reason why I was late is because I missed the bus.
entries.expected: I was late because I missed the bus.
entries.vietlishPattern: lý do tại sao tôi đến muộn là vì → 'lý do...là vì' structure calqued; 'the reason why...is because' is redundant in standard English

entries.input: I am not sure that whether she will come.
entries.expected: I am not sure whether she will come.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi không chắc là liệu cô ấy có đến không → 'là' (that) and 'liệu' (whether) both translated; choose one complementizer

entries.input: Because she was tired, so she went to bed early.
entries.expected: Because she was tired, she went to bed early.
entries.vietlishPattern: vì cô ấy mệt nên cô ấy đi ngủ sớm → 'vì...nên' double causal conjunction; English uses 'because' alone without a paired result connector
